subject: floatingIslandDiorama
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: floating sky island with ruins, waterfall and trees.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
Since this is a diorama rather than a creature, I don't need a skeleton, but I should still include a single root joint to satisfy the builder's requirements—I'll place one named "island" at the origin to be safe.

Since the model should rest on the floor at its lowest point, I'm treating this as a floating island diorama where the underside tip of the rock touches y=0 and everything builds upward from there. I'm sketching the scale now: roughly a 3m radius island with a jagged rock underside tapering to a point at the bottom, topped with grass around y=3.2, and total height including trees around 7m, using lathe geometry for the inverted rock cone with an outline profile defining the stalactite-like shape.

For the rock shape, I'm building an irregular lathe profile that goes from the axis out to the widest point near the top and back to the axis, using a low segment count to keep it faceted and low-poly rather than smooth. To break up the regularity I'm planning to scatter extra rock chunks—small cones and dodecahedrons—hanging off the main mass, and I'm thinking through the paint approach: layered strata along the vertical grain axis with earthy brown-grey tones, mottled, and a mossy countershade near the top where it meets the grass, all rendered in a clean pastel cel-shaded style using the toon kit's cel paint function.

Now I'm working out the grass-to-dirt transition on the island's underside, Genshin-style with a drooping lip of dirt between the grass cap and the rock body. I'm writing a custom paint function that uses the angle around the vertical axis to drive a zigzag pattern creating jagged grass-dirt boundary teeth, combined with some noise for organic variation, so the edge looks torn and natural rather than a perfect circle.

Since the top can't be perfectly flat with just a lathe, I'm planning to add gentle hill mounds using flattened spheres in grass colour, and I want to include a waterfall feature cascading off one edge of the island — built as a stream flowing from a small spring pool toward the front-left edge, then falling as a thin sheet past the rock face before dissolving into mist puffs below.

I'm figuring out the waterfall's appearance: a light cyan color with streak-like texture using stripe paints along the x-axis for a flowing water look, giving it some glow. For geometry, I'm positioning the falling sheet at the island's rim using polar coordinates to place it at the right azimuth angle on the rock edge.

The sheet falls straight down from the lip, staying clear of the rock as it narrows, down to around y=0.5 where it dissolves into mist puffs. I'm shaping it as a thin tapered extruded slab to give the falling water some natural variation in width.

Now I'm thinking about adding a stream ribbon running along the top from a spring near the ruins down to the lip, using a smooth curved path.

I'll keep the stream on the flat top area away from the hills, raising it slightly above the grass as a blue ribbon with bank stones along its sides, then work out the lip's cap radius.

Shifting the waterfall sheet to center at radial 3.12 so it straddles the cap edge properly, with the rock face narrowing below so the water appears to fall freely off the lip rather than hugging the rock. Now defining the cap lathe geometry...

Defining lathe profiles...

I'm also planning glowing cyan crystal clusters on the underside, plus ruin elements like a broken stone arch, columns, stairs, and a platform with an emblem decal evoking the Genshin anemo symbol. For vegetation, I'm thinking two stylized tree types—a pink-canopy sakura and a round teal tree—with a soft pastel palette tying everything together.

Now I'm filling in smaller details: grass tufts, glowing white/blue flowers, bushes, rocks, and a scattering of small floating rock fragments with crystal glow near the island. I want some mist near the waterfall and a few low clouds ringing the bottom rim, keeping everything above the floor level since nothing should hang below y=0.

With a target of 180-340 parts and 5-12 textures, I'm sketching the texture list: grass tuft cards, a small flower/petal card, a leaf cluster card for canopy edges, a glowing anemo rune decal for the ruins, and a plan for the waterfall using stacked planes or a custom striped paint since extrusion alone won't give the right look.

For the waterfall I'm designing a procedural paint function that creates vertical streaks with noise-based variation, blending cyan and white with foam highlighting near the top. Beyond that I'm adding a banner cloth texture for the ruin flag, hanging vine cards draping from the island rim, a stone tablet with glowing teal glyph inscriptions, and considering whether to include small extras like a torii or lantern.

Now I'm designing the ruins centerpiece itself: a broken gate with two pillars and a cracked lintel, stairs leading up to a circular altar platform inscribed with a glowing anemo emblem, a fallen column, a wall fragment with a window, and a floating glowing teal crystal with a ring hovering above the altar as the hero element. I'm setting up a coordinate helper that calculates ground height from gaussian hill bumps so I can place all these ruin pieces naturally into the island's terrain.

Working out grass color palettes...

Defining color palette and material rules...

For canopy blobs I'll use clumped icosahedron shapes with lighter mottled tops, scattering small leaf cards across the surface tinted by color so a single greyscale leaf texture can be reused with different tints.

For the joint hierarchy, I'll keep it minimal: a root joint plus maybe one extra joint for a floating orb crystal so I can bob it independently, rather than over-engineering separate joints for every tree or ruin piece.

To avoid unassigned geometry accidentally snapping to the wrong joint's bone segment, I'll make a small wrapper helper around part creation that always defaults bone to root unless I explicitly override it.

Actually, I decide the simplest fix is to only ever create a single root joint for the whole rig since props don't really need multi-joint animation — everything just attaches there by default, cutting the risk entirely. Now I'm starting to set up the imports and utility helpers for the builder module.

I'm estimating texel density across the painted island area to check resolution adequacy—around 150-200m² total surface at 1024 paint size gives roughly 60-70 texels per meter, which seems sufficient for crisp cel-shading boundaries.

Now I'm checking the API details for seeding randomness with rng(seed) returning a callable generator, and reviewing how the part() helper handles placement options like position, rotation in degrees, and scale vectors for orienting objects.

For the rock, I'm defining color constants and sketching a faceted lathe profile using irregular radius/height points to create a jagged, natural-looking rock silhouette with sharp creases rather than smooth curves.

Writing rock paint shader...

I'm noting that cel shading with the downward-facing light vector means the rock's underside normals mostly land in shadow, which reads fine for a dark underside but might look dull — considering lowering the threshold slightly for more tonal variety instead of a hard cutoff.

Now checking the cap lathe profile against the body's top radius — the cap's lower radius steps are close enough to the body's that there's a risk of a thin overlapping step where the cap bottom pokes slightly outside the body silhouette.

Each hill sphere needs its radius checked so it stays within the base cap's 3.1 radius boundary, adjusting sizes like shrinking the back-left hill's radius slightly so it doesn't poke past the lip, while confirming the sphere's lower half stays hidden inside the cap thickness.

Now I'm placing the waterfall stream's starting point on the lip. I'm working out the tangent and radial directions at that azimuth so the waterfall sheet faces outward correctly, then tracing the stream's path from a small spring pool near the ruins down to that lip point.
